This is a petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, by the accused persons in Crime No.525/2018 of Santhanpara Police Station,
Idukki, which is pending as CC. No.37/2018 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Nedumkandam.

The offences alleged against the petitioners are under Sections 406 and 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
2.

The prosecution case is that the accused persons including the petitioners herein with the intention to cheat the defacto complainant and to get unjust enrichment after offering job, received a sum of Rs.10,50,000/- through different bank accounts and thereafter failed to fulfill the promise and thereby cheated the defacto complainant.

3. According to the petitioners, the dispute has been amicably settled with the defacto complainant/victim/respondent No.3 and that she agreed to drop all further proceedings relating to the above dispute.

It is also submitted that as per judgment dated 18.6.2025 in Crl.M.C.
Praveen S vs State Of Kerala on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114660107/
2 No.5698/2022, this Court has quashed the case as against two other accused persons.

sentences.text:
Therefore,
they prayed for quashing all further proceedings against them.
4. The defacto complainant/victim filed affidavit endorsing the averments in the Criminal MC.
According to her, the dispute has been amicably settled and that she does not intend to proceed with the case and also that further proceedings in the case can be quashed.
She has no further grievance against the petitioners.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor, after getting instructions from the 2026:KER:27706 investigating officer also submitted that the dispute has been amicably settled between the parties and that the defacto complainant/victim is not interested in continuing the prosecution against the petitioners.

6. Considering the fact that the offences involved in this case are not heinous and very serious, but purely of private in nature and now the dispute has been settled between the parties, quashment of the same is necessary for maintaining harmonious relationship between the parties and also to prevent abuse of process of the court.

Moreover as per judgment dated 18.6.2025 in Crl.M.C.
No.5698/2022, this Court has quashed the case as against two other accused persons.
7. In the result, this Crl. M.C is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioners in CC.
No.37/2018 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Nedumkandam, arising from Crime No.525/2018 of Santhanpara Police Station,Idukki, stands quashed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
